newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index soars in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index soars in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumped 219 points or 1.74 percent to 12,819 at the opening on Wednesday following a surge on Wall Street overnight, brokers said.
The blue-chip index continued to rise, hitting a high of 12,924.27 before steadying at 12,880.90 up 280.48 points, after the first 20 minutes of trade. Turnover was HK$1.49 billion.

"There is some programme buying on blue chips, especially on HSBC Holdings," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities. He said buying was encouraged by the overnight rally on Wall Street.
The Dow industrials rose 179.01 points, or 2.64 percent to 6,962.03 after weaker-than-expected U.S. wage inflation data soothed concerns about rising interest rates.
Brokers said the 0.6 percent rise in the U.S. employment cost index in the first quarter released overnight was lower than market expectations of a 0.9 percent increase.
Ng said sentiment had improved slightly in both the United States and Hong Kong after the figure came out, and he believed any interest rate increase would be in the last quarter.
But other brokers were not so certain, saying the morning rally was just a knee jerk reaction to Wall Street.
"It is a good opportunity to unload some blue chips and switch to second and third liners," said a broker at OCBC Securities.
China-backed red chips and H-shares also rebounded in morning trading, with the Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index rising 18.43 points, or 1.77 percent to 1,058.36.
Brokers expected the recent consolidation by red-chips and H-shares to continue after a brief recovery since the counters, especially red-chips, had been overbought lately.
Among blue chips HSBC Holdings rose HK$4.0 to HK$194 and Hang Seng Bank added HK$2.25 to HK$87.
Brokers said buying on property remained relatively thin but Cheung Kong rose HK$2.0 to HK$68.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties jumped HK$3.0 to HK$83.75.
